## Conclusions
- **Distilling from a zero-shot teacher hurts.** Same data, steps, seed and recipe as the control (010), plus
  affinity distillation from PE-Core-L/14-336 (best single teacher in 009, 73.86 zero-shot) at alpha 0.5:
  RefCOCOg-LPCVC **81.74 vs 87.34** for the control. The paired delta vs 010 is **-5.60 [-6.9, -4.4]** (significant).
  On the LPCVC sample it is +0.62 [-0.7, +2.1] (noise).
- **Why:** the teacher has never seen this caption style. Its in-batch similarity distributions are worse than
  what the student learns from the labels within one epoch (85.2 after epoch 1 in 010), so the KL term pulls
  the student back toward the teacher's weaker ranking. Distillation only helps when the teacher is better *on the target task*.
- **Cost:** teacher embeddings (15,905 images × 2 flips + 65,306 captions) took 7 min once and are cached; training
  itself is no slower than 010 (5 min when the GPU is not shared).
- **Decision:** drop zero-shot-teacher distillation. If we revisit distillation, the teacher must first be
  fine-tuned on the same training data (a "fine-tuned teacher → student" run). This is optional and only
  worth it if the time budget allows.
